paragraphs: Rabbi Dosa ben Horkenos: Avot 3:10. He is mentioned in the Mishnah, Eruvin 39a; Rosh Hashanah 25a; chapter Dayyanei Gezerot, mishnayot 1 and 2, 107, end of side b, with Admon and Chanan ben Avishalom; Eduyot 3:1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; Chullin, beginning of chapter Reshit HaGez; Ohalot 3:1; Negaim 1:4. He lived more than 400 years: he was in Shimon the Righteous’s generation, as Maimonides writes at the end of Avot chapter 4 and in the introduction to order Zeraim, and throughout the Second Temple period until Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Akiva after the destruction. He was involved in the testimony concerning the new moon (see above, Gamliel of Yavneh), in the matter with Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah (see his entry). So too it appears in Yevamot chapter 1, 16a. Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, and Rabbi Akiva went to him; he seated them on gold couches. He addressed Rabbi Yehoshua as “my teacher.” He said, “Does our colleague Azaryah have a son?” He said to Rabbi Akiva, “Are you Akiva ben Yosef, whose name goes from one end of the world to the other?” He testified, “On this mortar sat Haggai the prophet.” This is Maimonides’ view. But this is difficult, for in chapter Hazorek Get, 81a, Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai said: “The earlier generations: Beit Shammai; the later generations: Rabbi Dosa, who said that a captive woman eats terumah.” So too in Eduyot chapter 3: Rabbi Dosa ben Horkenos said this. If he was before Beit Shammai, how is he among the later ones? Moreover, there in Yevamot it says that he had a younger brother named Yonatan (see his entry), one of Beit Shammai’s students. It is impossible that he too had a brother of 400 years. Perhaps his testimony that Haggai sat on this mortar was a tradition in his possession, rather than something he saw; or Haggai lived some two hundred years. Indeed, it appears that Rabbi Dosa lived a long life—נ״ב [unresolved]—for he was very old, until his eyes grew dim. But one cannot say that he lived in Shimon the Righteous’s days, as I wrote on a separate sheet. His burial and that of his father Horkenos are in a cave in Tzfat (G.A.Y.). Rabbi Eliezer was his brother. Regarding Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, Derekh Chayim is uncertain whether he was the son of Dosa ben Horkenos; see there, and see Rabbi Tzadok.
